From what I can tell, this is just the same PLA with hemp fibers as reinforcement. This won't cut it, as very few materials are suitable for airship design. Airships have to contend with the square-cubed law, which means that the available weight of the material that can be allocated to the skin grows disproportionately larger as the size of the craft increases. This means a few important things, one being that, for any given skin material, there exists a certain 'minimum size' below which the airship cannot carry any useful payload (remember, batteries / solar panels are heavy). Another is that the strength-to-weight of the skin material is the most important factor in choosing the material.

These concepts basically mean that, below a certain size, an airship must necessarily have a metallic foil skin, and above some threshold size will almost certainly be entirely of solid aluminum construction (no composite or laminate can compete with the 7000 series, and even the 2000 series bests all but the most exotic composites).

These materials aren't hard to work with or design for, but certainly won't be fused-deposition modeled anytime soon. And the required size of your first model would easily fill a small room.

Also, there are additional problems if you are planning to use a textile or other fabric as your skin.
